name: filmautomator
description: Autonomous AI filmmaking on Blender and FFmpeg: plan shots, build scenes, review renders, and produce a finished movie.
long_description:
FilmAutomator turns a plain-language objective into a finished film using software already on this machine.

Give it a creative brief and it plans shots, builds each one in Blender, renders a preview, hands you the actual image so you can judge it, corrects what you object to, renders at final quality, and assembles the result with FFmpeg.

**Blender is the renderer.** There is no AI video-generation model in this pipeline and none is required: you decide what should be created, Blender creates the actual pixels, FFmpeg encodes them.

**You are the director.** `render_shot_preview` returns the real rendered image, not a path to one. Look at it, then call `correct_shot` to change the camera, lens or lighting, and preview again.

**Storage is governed.** A configurable ceiling (35 GB by default) covers working artifacts. Frames are released only after a shot's MP4 has been encoded and verified, so a shot never loses its only copy.

**No paid services.** It runs entirely locally on Blender, FFmpeg, Python and SQLite. A model server (LM Studio, Ollama, llama.cpp) is optional: without one it falls back to a deterministic plan and judges frames from pixel measurement alone, labelling every synthetic decision as such.

**What it does not do.** This is a production tool, not a chat toy. It renders real frames, which takes real time — `start_production` returns immediately and the work continues in the background. Because a production owns a Blender session on one machine, only one runs at a time.

**Requirements on this machine.** Blender 4.x/5.x and FFmpeg must already be installed (`brew install --cask blender ffmpeg`). Use the `doctor` tool or `filmautomator doctor` to check.

The server speaks MCP over stdio and binds nothing to the network.

project_dir.title: FilmAutomator project folder
project_dir.description: The folder containing the 'filmautomator' package and the 'projects' output directory. This must be the checkout you want the extension to run, for example /Users/sahinsamrat/Downloads/blender.

python_path.title: Python 3 executable
python_path.description: Absolute path to the python3 that will run the server. Must be Python 3.11 or newer. Blender and FFmpeg are separate requirements and are checked by the 'doctor' tool.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create a new film project and return its project_id.

tools.name: start_production
tools.description: Begin producing a film in the background from a plain-language objective.

tools.name: render_shot_preview
tools.description: Render a shot preview and return the actual image so you can inspect it.

tools.name: correct_shot
tools.description: Change a shot's camera, lens or lighting after looking at its preview.

tools.name: finalize_shot
tools.description: Render, encode, verify a shot and release its frames once promoted.

tools.name: get_storage_status
tools.description: Working storage usage against the configurable ceiling, and what is reclaimable.

tools.name: get_production_status
tools.description: Current run state, progress, current shot and what the agents are doing.

tools.name: get_preview
tools.description: The latest rendered preview for a shot, as an actual image.

tools.name: get_final_movie
tools.description: The finished film: path, duration, resolution, frame rate and codec.
